bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction, digitoxin vs placebo reduced the primary composite of death from any cause or first hospital admission for worsening heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98).
implications: These data support that, in the modified intention-to-treat population, digitoxin was associated with a lower hazard of the composite endpoint of death from any cause or first hospital admission for worsening heart failure than placebo (hazard ratio 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98; P=0.03). The confidence interval for death from any cause includes 1.0 (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.69 to 1.07), so the document does not establish superiority for all-cause mortality alone; it reports noninferiority (threshold 1.303; P<0.001). Serious adverse events occurred in 4.7% with digitoxin vs 2.8% with placebo.

major_points.text: International, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase 4 trial at 65 sites.
major_points.quote: We conducted this phase 4, double-blind, ran- domized, placebo-controlled trial at 65 sites in Austria, Germany, and Serbia.

major_points.text: Eligibility required symptomatic chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and specified NYHA class, on evidence-based therapy for at least 6 months.
major_points.quote: Patients were eligible for enrollment if they were at least 18 years old, had symptomatic chronic heart failure (specified as a left ventricular ejec- tion fraction of <40% and an NYHA functional class of III or IV, or a left ventricular ejection frac- tion of <30% and an NYHA functional class of ID, and had received evidence-based therapy for heart failure for a period of at least 6 months.

major_points.text: Intervention was digitoxin starting dose 0.07 mg once daily with blinded serum-based dose adjustment to a target range.
major_points.quote: Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive digitoxin at a starting dose of 0.07 mg once daily or matching placebo. Dose adjustments were made according to a predefined algorithm: digitoxin concentrations in serum were measured in a blinded manner

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause or hospital admission for worsening heart failure (first event).
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause or hospital admission for worsening heart failure, whichever occurred first.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred less often with digitoxin than placebo over a median follow-up of 36 months (HR 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98; P=0.03).
major_points.quote: Over a median follow-up of 36 months, a primary-outcome event occurred in 242 patients (39.5%) in the digitoxin group and 264 (44.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for death or first hospital admission for worsening heart failure, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.98; P=0.03).

major_points.text: At least one serious adverse event was more frequent in the digitoxin group than the placebo group (4.7% vs 2.8%).
major_points.quote: At least one serious adverse event occurred in 29 patients (4.7%) in the digitoxin group and 17 (2.8%) in the placebo group.

analysis_methods.text: Efficacy analyses performed in a modified intention-to-treat population excluding randomized patients confirmed to have never taken assigned treatment.

analysis_methods.text: Primary analysis used a Cox regression model with assigned group and randomization strata as independent variables.
analysis_methods.quote: the superiority of digitoxin to placebo with re- spect to death from any cause or hospitalization for worsening heart failure, whichever occurred first, was tested in a Cox regression model with assigned group (digitoxin or placebo) and ran- domization strata as independent variables.

analysis_methods.text: Planned sample size was 2190 patients and 734 events for 80% power for superiority on the primary outcome.
analysis_methods.quote: We calculated that a sample of 2190 patients and 734 events would provide the trial with 80% power to show superiority of digitoxin to placebo with respect to the primary outcome.
